intro:
*** CZECH LEGION - SIBERIAN ANABASIS ***

Our beloved lands of Bohemia and Moravia have been under Habsburg control for centuries. Now, during the World War, the time has come to liberate ourselves and rule our own country ourselves!

The Habsburg K.u.K Army has suffered tremendous losses ever since 1914 and of the hundreds of thousands prisoners, a considerable number of Czech were part of that. Our political leaders, like Masaryk and Durich, have received permission from the Russian Tsar to form a Czech Legion. In 1916 two Czech regiments were formed. Early 1917 a revolution takes place in Russia which forces the Tsar to abdicate. Under the new government, lead by Kerensky, Russia continues the war against Austria-Hungary and the Germany. The Czech Legion is expanded to brigade size and is deployed at the southern front against the Austro-Hungarian K.u.K Army in the area of Zborow when Kerensky orders an offensive.

00. ZBOROW (2 July 1917)

The Czech Legion will take part in the Kerensky Offensive, lead by the 1916 hero Brusilov. The goal is to capture Lemberg and Kowel. The Czech Legion receives orders to capture the village of Pluhiv after breaking through the Austro-Hungarian trenches.

The Czech Legion is deployed in between the Finnish 6th and 4th divisions. The Austro-Hungarian forces consist of the K.u.K. 19th infantry division which consists roughly of half of Czechs... Success is vital!

briliant.text:
OUTCOME

The Czech action at Zborow was a huge success for the Czech Legion. The Russian Army was weary of three years of defeat after defeat and were deeply demoralized. So were the Austro-Hungarian forces at the other side. Two of the Austrian regiments had more than 50% of Czechs filling the ranks.

In the battle of Zborow the Czech Legion captured 62 officers, 3150 soldiers, 15 canons and lots of machine guns. The losses were only 185 killed and 800 wounded. Though in general, the Kerensky offensive was a failure, the Czechs proved their worth and spirit in battle.

The Czech victory was kept silent in the Habsburg Empire but was made public in almost all other countries, including Germany. Kerensky allowed the Legion to expand and conduct an independant offensive which had minimum success. The front kept quiet the coming months when another revolution, the Bolshevik revolution, took place in Russia broke out...

intro:
01. Kiev (28 February 1918)

The Bolshevik rule in Russia had resulted in a armistice with the Central Powers signed on 17 December 1917. At the moment peace talks are taking place in Brest-Litovsk. To force the Bolsheviks to sign, the Central Powers have resumed their offensive actions and because of the complete dissarray of the Russian Army, they are pushing deep into the Ukraine. At the time, the Czech Legion was retreating east to avoid capture by the German Army. The Czech Legion was now an independant force, obeying only to their own commander as nobody else could be trusted.

Near the end of February 1918 the German Army had reached the outskirts of the Ukrainian capitol of Kiev. The Bolshevik authorities have fled the city leaving only behind the most fanatical volunteers. Ukrainian nationalist are welcoming the Germans as liberators of their country. One of the German goals is to capture or destroy the Czech Legion for it was that force that was essential in slowing down the German advance time after time.

As we speak the Czech Legion has partly reached Kiev and parts of the Legion will take up defensive positions at the bridges over the Dnjepr River, so that the bulk of Czech Legion can retreat even deeper into the Ukraine and stay out of German hands. You will have to hold out for at least five days.

NOTE: After 11 turns you must hold 3 VHs to win the scenario.

briliant.text:
OUTCOME

The German juggernaut into the Ukraine was in general unstoppable because the Imperial Russian Army was no more. Only scattered troops were fleeing to safety. Chaos was complete. Kiev was evacuated by the Bolsheviks as soon as the Germans came near.

The Czech Legion was also retreating east to stay out of German hands. The Legion's 2nd Regiment took up positions at the bridges over the Dnjepr River at Kiev and held these for five days, until 3 March 1918, so that the bulk of the Czech Legion could retreat east. The 2nd regiment then broke off contact and joined the Legion again. Kiev was now in German hands but the Czech Legion had escaped!

intro:
02. BACHMATSJ (13 March 1918)

On 3 March 1918 the Bolsheviks signed the peace treaty of Brest-Litovsk which made an end to official hostilities between Russia and the Central Powers. However sporadic fighting continued for days. Russia gave away huge territories including the Ukraine. At the time of the armistice the Czech Legion was east of Kiev.

The Germans were close to reaching their new borders on the border of Russia and the Ukraine. German forces made rapid advances using the railways. A collision between German troops and the Czech Legion is about to take place near the village of Bachmatsj, between Kiev and Konotop. To avoid capture it might be needed to fight a way east. Soviet Red Army troops are in the same position and are also trying to flee east. Cooperation with the Communists could be useful to our cause.

briliant.text:
OUTCOME

At Bachmatsj the Czech Legion, in cooperation with Soviet Red Army units, stopped the advance of the German Army and could march its way east, out of the German occupied regions of Russia.

Seeing no future staying in Russia, the Czech Legion decided to get out of Russia somehow. Ultimately the plan would be to travel across Siberia, using the Trans-Siberian railway, to reach Wladiwostok and embark to France. In the weeks after the action at Bachmatsj, the Legion was dispersed at the railways between Penza and the Ural mountains.

intro:
03. TSJELJABINSK (14 May 1918)

An agreement has been made between the Bolshevik authorities in Moscow and the Czech Legion. The Legion is allowed to get out of Russia using the Trans-Siberian railway. So the Legion was scattered over the railway between Penza and the Urals in May 1918.

It was not of the Legion's wishes to mix itself into any Russian internal affairs but local Soviet authorities were sometimes acting on their own good. The relation between the Soviets and Czechs was tense. So on 14 May 1918 the units of the Legion arrived in Tsjeljabinsk, east of the Ural mountains, where a train with Hungarian prisoners of war which were returning to Austria-Hungary in accordance with the Brest-Litovsk treaty. At Tsjeljabinsk an incident between a number of Czechs and Hungarians took place after which the local Soviet authority imprisoned a number of Czechs. Trotsky ordered to disarm the Legion which was sufficient for the Legion's commanders to take their faith into their own hands.

You have to attack the prisonhouse in Tsjeljabinsk and free your fellow legionairs. You might have to defend yourself against possible attacking local Soviet troops and the Hungarian POWs which are still in the vicinity. Parts of the Legion is still at railroads west of Tsjejabinsk but some of them might arrive on time to help you.

NOTE: YOU CAN USE THE RAILROADS BY EMBARKING YOUR UNITS FROM NOW ON.

briliant.text:
OUTCOME

With the Czech action at Tsjeljabinsk the imprisoned Legionairs were freed. Even more, the Soviet rule in the city was destroyed. The Legion would take care of their own way how to reach Wladiswostok and get out of Russia. No longer it would cooperate with the Soviet authorities. Still the Legion was scattered from Penza, west of the Volga River, to Tsjeljabinsk, east of the Urals...

intro:
04. SAMARA (26 May 1918)

After breaking with the Soviet authorities, the Czech Legion started to take over city after city along the railroads towards Wladiwostok. As it was still dispersed from east of the Urals in the east to almost the Volga River in the west. Before long the Legion held power over a huge stretch of territory and was seen as one of the most dangerous enemies by the Soviet leaders in Moscow. In an attempt to secure itself the Czech Legion carried out attacks on Soviet cities. Tsjeljabinsk and Ufa had already been taken. Samara on the Volga River would be next.

Your are ordered to use the railroads to reach Samara on the Volga River. No doubt the Soviets will attempt to slow you down on the way to buy time to prepare defenses of Samara. You veterans must overcome all difficulties and clear Samara from Bolsheviks.

briliant.text:
OUTCOME

The Legion succesfully occupied Samara and was threatening more Russian cities along the Volga. Through foreign and through White Russian eyes, the Legion was an ideal force for the counter-revolution and overthrow the Soviets. However the Czech Legion was fighting its own struggle and it only occasionally co-operated with White Russian authorities.

intro:
05. KAZAN (7 July 1918)

In the process of securing its own fate, the Czech Legion was capturing various cities. Within weeks the Volga River was reached and the city of Samara was taken. Next would be Kazan, famous for holding the Imperial Gold Reserve. A fact not lost for the Czech Legion.

From Samara, south of Kazan, you will once again use the railroad system to quickly reach Kazan and clear it of Bolsheviks. The Imperial Gold Reserve is also one of your goals. If we capture it, we have a very good negitiation position - with anyone.

briliant.text:
OUTCOME

Bolshevik power in Kazan was overthrown and the Czech Legion captured eight train cars of gold.

Furthermore, the loss of Kazan shocked Soviet authorities in Moscow and the Czech Legion was seen as one of the many enemies of the Communist rule in Russia.

intro:
07. OMSK (22 December 1918)

The autumn of 1918 brought good news to the Czech Legion. Austria-Hungary had surrendered and the new state of Czechoslovakia had declared its independance. In short, the Czechs and Slovaks of the Legion had a home to attend to. It would no longer be unneccasarily involve itself in the Russian Civil War anymore.

To reach its homeland, the Legion had still to cross Siberia, which was in control of White Russian power under Admiral Koltsjak. December 1918 saw a revolt against Koltsjak in Omsk, east of the Ural mountains, where Koltsjak held court. The Czech Legion supported Koltsjak as he did not object to the presence the Czech Legion - both sides had profit from one another.

A small part of the Legion will take part in the action to put down this revolt. Support will come from Cossacks which are grazing in the countryside.

briliant.text:
OUTCOME

The revolt was crushed. Almost 500 rebels were executed. Some of the opponents eventually joined the Soviets. Koltsjak's regime, however, was secured.

intro:
09. SEMENOV (10 February 1920)

Early 1920, the Legion was close to reaching Wladiwostok. At Irkutsk the Czech Legion traded the Imperial Gold Reserve and Koltsjak to the Soviets for a free passage further east. Being already east of Lake Baikal, it was thought no more fighting would take place. However these regions, east of Lake Baikal, were never under control by Koltsjak and a Cossack ruler, Ataman Semenov, ruled here. Semenov was supported by Japan and was initially hostile towards the Legion.

You must go further east towards Chita. Our goal remains leaving Russia and get home. Semenov's Transbaikal Cossacks might try to stop you and you have orders not to be stopped by anyone.

briliant.text:
OUTCOME

After several clashes with Ataman Semenov, Semenov left the Czechs for what they were and concentrated on the Soviet forces which were approaching. The Czech Legion was steaming full speed on Wladiwostok!

intro:
10. WLADIWOSTOK (10 March 1920)

After two years of struggle getting through Russia, the Czech Legion had finally reached Wladiwostok and all what was left was waiting on ships to take them home, as initially there were not sufficient ships to take all back home at once.

You have get to Wladiswostok by passing American and Japanese zones of occupation. No more fighting is needed! You are going home!!!

briliant.text:
OUTCOME

After Wladiwostok was reached, it took months to get home. Partly because there still had be ships to arrive to take them on board, partly because of a huge journey from the Pacific Ocean to European ports, and from there over land to the new republic of Czechoslovakia: HOME!

intro:
06. KAZAN - RED OFFENSIVE (27 October 1918)

The loss of Kazan had generated into enormous bolshevik activity to stop the Czech Legion from capturing more cities and advance across the Volga River towards Moscow. Leon Trotski himself would conduct the preparations.

The Soviet assembled their Fifth Army under General Tukhachevsky, which later lead the invasion of Poland and become victim of Stalin's purges. The Fifth Army had reached the Volga River and was now ready to recapture Kazan.

You must hold Kazan and hold the enemy at bay. We have no intentions of advancing towards Moscow but we will not be defeated. Also hold open the railroads to the Ural mountains.

briliant.text:
OUTCOME

The Soviets eventually captured Kazan and the Czech Legion would retreat. News from Europe would weaken the wrath against the bolsheviks...

intro:
08. UFA (9 June 1919)

The Czech Legion had withdrawn itself from the Russian Civil War and was only sparsely involved when 1918 ended. However, still elements of the Legion were scattered as far west as Ufa, near the Ural mountains, when the White Russian forces of Koltsjak were on the retreat under pressure of a huge Soviet offensive aimed at destroying the White Russians in Siberia.

The White Russian Siberian Army has suffered defeat after defeat and is retreating towards to Ural mountains where it hopes to stop the Soviet advance. The important city of Ufa has just now fallen in Soviet hands. Czech Legion units are near Ufa and are in immediately threat of being attacked.

You are in command of the Czech Legion units near Ufa. You must hold any enemy from blocking the railroads going east, to the Ural mountains and safeguard the railroad. It might be needed to engage Soviet units because the White Russian army might not be able to stem the Soviet advance...

briliant.text:
OUTCOME

The Czech Legion was only sparsely involved in the battles between the Red Army and the White Russian Siberian Army. The White Russians lead defeat after defeat and near the end of 1919 the Red Army had captured Siberia all the way to Omsk. By then, the Czech Legion was already in eastern Siberia...
